title: The night of the fireflies
summary: At Grandma's house, a little girl can't get to sleep. Grandma teaches her a trick: counting fireflies.

scenes.text:
At Grandma's house, summer nights were very quiet.

No cars went by. No dogs barked. All you could hear was the countryside, breathing softly.

Ana lay in bed with her eyes wide open. She turned over. She turned over again. It was no use.

Then she saw something through the window.

A tiny light, in the garden. It came on, and went out.

Then another, a little further away. And another.

Ana sat up in bed.

"Grandma," she called softly. "There are lights in the garden."

Grandma didn't tell her to go to sleep. Grandma put on her dressing gown, took her hand, and they went down to the garden together.

Ana was barefoot. The grass was cool and tickled between her toes.

The lights were everywhere. Among the flowers, over the grass, in the low branches of the lemon tree. They lit up and went dark, each at its own pace, as if they were talking to each other.

"They're fireflies," said Grandma. "They come out on the quietest nights."

One flew close and landed on Ana's finger. It was tiny. It lit up, warm, right on top of her fingernail.

"Hello," Ana told it, in a whisper.

Grandma sat down on the garden bench, and Ana sat on her lap.

"Do you know what I do when I can't sleep?" she said. "I count them."

"The fireflies?"

"Every time one lights up, you count one. Nice and slowly."

Ana looked out over the garden.

One.

Two.

Three, next to the lemon tree.

Four… five…

Her eyes were getting heavy.

Six.

Grandma never heard seven. When she looked down, Ana was curled up against her chest, breathing slowly, fast asleep.

She carried her to bed without waking her. And out in the garden, the fireflies kept lighting up, one by one, in case anyone else needed counting.
